statement: Ana can paint a fence by herself in $4$ hours, Ben can paint it by himself in $6$ hours, and Cal can paint it by himself in $12$ hours. Ana starts painting at 9:00 a.m. Ben joins her at 10:00 a.m., and Cal joins them at 10:30 a.m. Each person works at a steady rate until the fence is finished. At what time is the fence finished?

choices.misconception: I treated all three as starting together at 9:00. Together they paint $\frac12$ of the fence per hour, so I got 2 hours and 11:00 a.m.
I counted the half hour from 10:00 to 10:30 as a full hour of Ana and Ben working, so I had $\frac14 + \frac{5}{12} = \frac23$ done by 10:30 and $40$ more minutes to go.
I had Cal join at 10:00 along with Ben, so after Ana's $\frac14$ the other $\frac34$ took $1.5$ hours at $\frac12$ fence per hour.
I forgot that Ana worked alone from 9:00 to 10:00, so I started the job at 10:00 and had $\frac{19}{24}$ left at 10:30, which took $95$ more minutes.

hints: Think of each person's speed as the fraction of the fence they paint in one hour.
Ana paints $\frac14$ of the fence per hour, Ben $\frac16$ and Cal $\frac{1}{12}$. Work out how much is painted by 10:00 and by 10:30.
By 10:30, $\frac14 + \frac{5}{24} = \frac{11}{24}$ of the fence is painted. All three together paint $\frac12$ of the fence per hour, so find how long the last $\frac{13}{24}$ takes.

solutions.reliable: In fences per hour, Ana paints $\frac14$, Ben $\frac16$ and Cal $\frac{1}{12}$. From 9:00 to 10:00 Ana alone paints $\frac14$. From 10:00 to 10:30, Ana and Ben paint at $\frac14 + \frac16 = \frac{5}{12}$ per hour for half an hour, which is $\frac{5}{24}$. By 10:30 the painted part is $\frac{6}{24} + \frac{5}{24} = \frac{11}{24}$, leaving $\frac{13}{24}$. All three together paint $\frac14 + \frac16 + \frac{1}{12} = \frac12$ of the fence per hour, so the rest takes $\frac{13}{24} \div \frac12 = \frac{13}{12}$ hours, which is $65$ minutes. The fence is finished at 11:35 a.m.
solutions.elegant: Pretend the fence has $12$ equal sections. Ana paints $3$ sections per hour, Ben $2$ and Cal $1$. By 10:00 Ana has painted $3$ sections, and from 10:00 to 10:30 Ana and Ben add $2.5$, for $5.5$. The last $6.5$ sections at $6$ sections per hour take $\frac{6.5}{6}$ hours, which is $65$ minutes, so they finish at 11:35 a.m.
